text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it was probing a series of agreements between U.S. computer giant IBM and Italian telecommunications group Stet.
It said the agreements were submitted for regulatory approval in the European Union on April 10 under EU rules banning accords which restrict fair competition or abuse of a dominant position.

Under the terms of the alliance announced in December, IBM appoints Telecom Italia SpA, a subsidiary of Stet, to market on a non-exclusive basis IBM Global Network (IGN) services in Italy, the Commission said in a notice published in the EU's Official Journal.
In a related agreement, Telecom Italia would acquire control of Intesa, a joint venture between IBM Semea SpA and FIAT SpA which is currently IGN's service provider in Italy, the Commission added.
IBM also appointed TMI Telemedia International Ltd, which belongs to Telecom Italia, to market IGN services internationally on a non-exclusive basis.
Finally, IBM and Stet have also agreed to develop business opportunities in the sector for digital video broadcasting.
There is no deadline for the Commission to rule on the agreements.
It called on interested parties to give their views. -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841
